lessons.title: Lesson 1: Using AI with money safely
lessons.text:
Lesson 1 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Prepare financial data so you can get AI help without exposing private details.
This lesson builds toward: Given a month of exported transactions, you will prepare the data for AI by removing account numbers and replacing names with labels, with no private financial details left, and AI math checked in the spreadsheet.
AI assistants are good at spreadsheet formulas, sorting, finding patterns and explaining terms like "accrual" or "gross margin". They are not accountants, can make math mistakes, and do not know tax rules for your exact situation.
Never paste bank or card numbers, routing numbers, passwords, Social Security or tax ID numbers, or names of customers, donors or employees into a general AI tool. Instead, export transactions to a spreadsheet, delete those columns, and replace names with general labels like "Customer A" or "Supplier 1".
Check AI math with the spreadsheet itself. Ask the AI for a formula, then let the spreadsheet calculate, and spot-check a few totals by hand. For tax, payroll and legal questions, confirm with irs.gov, your state tax agency or a licensed accountant.
Step by step:
- Export transactions from your bank or bookkeeping tool to a spreadsheet.
- Delete account numbers and any ID numbers.
- Replace people's names with labels like "Customer A".
- Use AI for formulas and explanations, not final tax answers.
- Spot-check AI math with the spreadsheet.
Words to know:
- Export: save information from one program into a file another program can open.
- Transaction: one money movement in or out, like a sale or a bill paid.
Try it now: Export or type 20 transactions from a real or sample month into a spreadsheet. Remove every account number and replace names with labels.
You can now prepare money data for AI help without exposing private details.

check.q: Which column should you delete before pasting transactions into an AI tool?
check.why: Account numbers are private and must never go into a general AI tool.

check.q: Your transactions list a customer named "Maria Lopez". What do you do before asking AI for help?
options: Leave the name; AI keeps it private
Replace it with a label like "Customer A"
check.why: Replacing names with labels protects privacy while AI still helps.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Sorting income and expenses into categories
lessons.text:
Lesson 2 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Use AI to suggest categories and a spreadsheet to total each one.
This lesson builds toward: Given your cleaned transactions and a category list, you will sort each transaction into a category and total each one with SUMIF, so the category totals add up to the full total.
Categories turn a long list of transactions into a picture. Common business categories: sales, cost of goods (ingredients, supplies for products), rent, payroll, marketing, software, vehicle and fuel, insurance and fees. Nonprofits often add donations, grants, program costs and fundraising costs.
Paste the cleaned description and amount columns into an AI assistant and ask: "Suggest a category for each line from this list: [your categories]. Return a table." Then copy the table back into your sheet and fix any it got wrong.
Ask AI for the formula to total each category. In both Google Sheets and Excel, SUMIF adds up amounts that match a label, for example =SUMIF(C:C, "Rent", D:D).
Step by step:
- Write your category list.
- Ask AI to suggest a category for each cleaned transaction.
- Paste the categories into your sheet and correct mistakes.
- Use SUMIF to total each category.
- Check that the category totals add up to the full total.
Words to know:
- Category: a group of similar transactions, like rent or marketing.
- SUMIF: a spreadsheet formula that adds amounts that match a condition.
- Cost of goods: what you spend to make or buy the products you sell.
Try it now: Have AI suggest categories for your 20 cleaned transactions, correct them, and total each category with SUMIF. Confirm the totals match the overall total.
You can now sort transactions into categories and total them with a spreadsheet formula.

check.q: What does SUMIF do in a spreadsheet?
options: Adds up amounts that match a label
check.why: SUMIF adds the amounts whose label matches, such as all Rent rows.

check.q: Your category totals add up to $4,800, but the full total is $5,000. What do you do?
options: Find the transactions that are missing a category or have the wrong label
Ask AI to make the numbers match
check.why: Category totals should equal the full total, so look for missing or mislabeled lines.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Building a budget and comparing it to actual
lessons.text:
Lesson 3 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: Build a monthly budget and a budget-versus-actual table that shows where you are off.
This lesson builds toward: Given a monthly budget and the actual totals, you will create a budget-versus-actual table with variance and percent off, with the three biggest variances explained in one sentence each.
A budget is your plan for money in and out for a period. Budget versus actual compares the plan to what really happened. The difference is called the variance.
Set up columns: category, budget, actual, variance (actual minus budget) and percent off. Ask AI: "Give me Google Sheets formulas for variance and percent variance." Then look for the biggest variances, in dollars and in percent.
Explain each big variance in one sentence. "Fuel was $300 over budget because we added a second delivery route." AI can help you word explanations, but only you know the real reasons.
Step by step:
- List categories with a budget amount for each.
- Bring in the actual totals from Lesson 2.
- Add variance = actual minus budget.
- Add percent off = variance divided by budget.
- Explain the three biggest variances in one sentence each.
Words to know:
- Budget: a plan for money coming in and going out.
- Variance: the difference between the budget and what really happened.
Try it now: Build a budget-versus-actual table for your month with variance and percent off. Explain the three biggest variances in one sentence each.
You can now build a budget, compare it to actual results and explain the differences.

check.q: In budget versus actual, how is variance calculated in this course?
Supplies were $200 over budget. AI suggests "prices went up", but you know you bought extra for an event. What do you write?
options: The real reason: extra supplies bought for the event
AI's reason, since it sounds fine
check.why: Only you know the real reason; AI can help with wording, not the facts.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Forecasting cash flow for the next 13 weeks
lessons.text:
Lesson 4 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: Build a 13-week cash flow forecast and find the week money is tightest.
This lesson builds toward: Given today's cash and expected money in and out, you will build a 13-week cash flow forecast and mark the lowest week, with each week's ending cash carried to the next week.
Profit and cash are not the same. You can be profitable on paper and still run out of cash if customers pay late or a big bill comes due. A cash flow forecast shows when money comes in and goes out, week by week.
A 13-week forecast (about three months) is a common tool. Rows: starting cash, cash in (sales, payments, donations, grants), cash out (payroll, rent, suppliers, loan payments), and ending cash. Each week's ending cash becomes next week's starting cash.
Ask AI to build the template: "Make a 13-week cash flow forecast table for Google Sheets with formulas where each week's ending cash becomes the next week's starting cash." Fill in your expected numbers, then find the lowest week. That is when you may need to delay a purchase, chase a payment or arrange a line of credit.
Step by step:
- Ask AI for a 13-week cash flow template with formulas.
- Enter today's cash balance as week 1 starting cash.
- Enter expected cash in and cash out for each week.
- Check that ending cash carries to the next week.
- Mark the lowest week and plan for it.
Words to know:
- Cash flow: the timing of money coming in and going out.
- Forecast: a best estimate of future numbers.
- Line of credit: a set amount a bank lets you borrow when needed.
Try it now: Build a 13-week cash flow forecast with AI's help. Fill in real or sample numbers and mark the lowest week with one action you would take.
You can now build a 13-week cash flow forecast and plan for the tightest week.

check.q: What does a cash flow forecast show?
options: When money comes in and goes out, week by week
check.why: A cash flow forecast shows money in and out week by week.

check.q: Your forecast shows cash below zero in week 7. What could you do?
options: Nothing; it is only a forecast
Delay a purchase, chase a payment or arrange a line of credit
check.why: The lowest week is when you plan ahead to cover the gap.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Spotting problems and fraud with AI
lessons.text:
Lesson 5 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Use AI and simple checks to spot unusual spending, duplicates and scams.
This lesson builds toward: Given a cleaned month of transactions and payment requests, you will identify possible duplicates, unusual spending and payment scams, confirming any bank-detail change by calling a number you already know.
AI and spreadsheets can flag things a busy person misses: duplicate payments, a subscription you forgot, a sudden jump in a category, or a vendor you do not recognize.
Ask: "Look at this cleaned table. List possible duplicates, unusual amounts and categories that changed a lot from last month." Then investigate each item yourself.
Watch for scams aimed at businesses and nonprofits: fake invoices, emails asking you to change a vendor's bank details, and urgent payment requests that seem to come from the boss. Always confirm by calling a phone number you already know. Report fraud at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.
Step by step:
- Ask AI to list possible duplicates and unusual amounts.
- Compare categories to last month.
- Investigate each flag yourself.
- Confirm any bank-detail change by calling a known number.
- Report fraud to the FTC.
Words to know:
- Duplicate payment: paying the same bill twice.
- Invoice: a bill asking for payment.
- Payment fraud: tricking someone into sending money to the wrong place.
Official sources:
- FTC: ReportFraud.ftc.gov
- FTC: How to recognize and avoid phishing scams
Try it now: Ask AI to review your cleaned transactions for duplicates and unusual amounts. Investigate each flag and write what you found.
You can now use AI and simple checks to spot unusual spending and payment scams.

check.q: Which is a common scam aimed at businesses and nonprofits?
options: A bank statement arriving by mail
An email asking you to change a vendor's bank details
check.why: Requests to change a vendor's bank details are a common scam.

check.q: AI flags two equal payments to the same vendor on the same day. What do you do?
options: Assume AI is right and cancel both
Investigate it yourself, such as checking the invoices
Pay the vendor a third time
check.why: AI flags possible problems; you investigate each one yourself.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Explaining the numbers and keeping good records
lessons.text:
Lesson 6 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Write a plain-language money update and know how long to keep records.
This lesson builds toward: Given your spreadsheet results, you will write a five-sentence plain-language money update and plan how long to keep the records, with every number checked against the spreadsheet.
Owners, partners and boards need a short, clear update, not a giant spreadsheet. A good update has five sentences: how much came in, how much went out, the biggest variance and why, the cash outlook from your forecast, and one decision or action needed.
Ask AI to turn your numbers into a draft, then check every figure against the spreadsheet. Remove anything AI added that is not true.
Keep records. The IRS says to keep records that support income and deductions until the period of limitations for that return runs out, generally 3 years, with longer periods in some cases and at least 4 years for employment tax records. Check irs.gov or an accountant for your situation.
Step by step:
- Write five sentences: in, out, biggest variance, cash outlook, decision needed.
- Have AI tidy the wording.
- Check every number against the spreadsheet.
- Save the spreadsheet and receipts in a safe, backed-up folder.
- Check irs.gov for how long to keep them.
Words to know:
- Board: the group that oversees a nonprofit or company.
- Period of limitations: the time the IRS has to review or change a tax return.
Official sources:
- IRS: How long should I keep records?
Try it now: Final task: write a five-sentence money update from your categorized month, budget-versus-actual table and 13-week forecast. Check every number, then save all files in a backed-up folder.
You can now organize, plan and explain an organization's money with AI help while keeping data safe.
How your final task is checked:
What we look at Not yet Meets Exceeds Private details removed The data still has account numbers, ID numbers or real names. All account and ID numbers removed and names replaced with labels. Can show how AI math was spot-checked in the spreadsheet. Categories and totals Transactions are not sorted, or totals do not match the full total. Every transaction has a category, SUMIF totals each one, and they add up to the full total. AI's wrong categories were found and corrected, with a note of which ones. Budget versus actual No variance column, or the big variances are not explained. Variance and percent off for each category, and the three biggest explained in one sentence each. Each explanation says what will be done about it next month. 13-week forecast Ending cash does not carry to the next week, or the lowest week is not marked. 13 weeks with cash in, cash out and ending cash carried forward, and the lowest week marked. Includes a plan for the lowest week. Money update Missing, longer than needed, or has numbers that do not match the sheet. Five sentences: in, out, biggest variance, cash outlook and a decision, all matching the sheet. Clear enough for someone with no finance background, and says where records are kept. To pass: Meets or Exceeds on every row. If a row is Not yet, fix that part and try again.

check.q: Which belongs in a five-sentence money update?
options: The cash outlook from your forecast
check.why: The update covers in, out, the biggest variance, the cash outlook and a decision needed.

check.q: AI's draft update says income rose 20%, but your sheet shows 12%. What do you do?
options: Correct it to match the spreadsheet before sending
check.why: Check every figure against the spreadsheet and remove anything that is not true.
